name: Water
summary: Water is what most of the body is made of: about 60% of an adult’s weight. It carries what the blood carries, keeps body temperature steady through sweat, and leaves mostly as urine. An adult needs about 2 to 2.5 litres a day from everything drunk and eaten, food giving about a fifth of it, and more in heat, with exercise or with a fever.
advisory: Too much water, too fast, dilutes the sodium in the blood (hyponatremia, or water intoxication). It starts with a headache, nausea, vomiting and confusion, can go on to seizures and coma, and can kill. MDMA makes the body hold on to water: sip no more than about 500 mL an hour while dancing, less while resting. Someone who is confused or vomiting after drinking a lot of water needs an ambulance, not more water.
doseBasis: Amounts are for one hour. Healthy kidneys pass about 0.8 to 1 litre an hour at most, so drinking more than that, hour after hour, waters down the blood.
